clips.text: You step off the kerb — and your shoe stays dry.
He takes another step. Still dry. He crosses the whole puddle, then the whole street, without one splash.
Look at his feet. Each foot slaps the water faster than you can blink — and the water holds him up, one slap at a time.
Now he crosses a whole river, dry shoes, dry socks, while the crowd on the bridge stares. But he never slows down. Not once.
So why can’t he stop — not for one second?
The answer is one number — and it changes everything.
Thirty metres a second — and the one pause that sinks you. Tap the video link under my name.
